Not that I believe the aircraft described in this patent will come to life, but after a quick google search I found that the SR-71's cruising altitude is 85,000 feet. The cruising altitude of this aircraft was said to be 100,000 feet.

Using the table on this page: http://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/standard-atmosphere-d_604.html

You can see that the absolute pressure at 80,000 ft is 0.406 lb/in^2.

At 100,000 ft the pressure is 0.162, which is ~40% the amount of air the nose will have to move out of the way compared to the SR-71.
